posts.title: Letting an AI write to your cap table: the rules it can't get around
posts.text:
Capfolder 0.1.5 works from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex and Gemini CLI. Your AI reads the cap table and shows a preview of every change.

The catch is trust. An AI that adds up shares on its own, or writes to your records without asking, is worse than no AI. So your AI uses Capfolder, and Capfolder keeps the math and the final say:

• Preview, then yes. A change is written only after you confirm the exact preview you were shown. A preview expires after 10 minutes, and it's refused if the folder changed in between.
• Capfolder does the math. Your AI never adds up shares itself.
• Every record is checked against the Open Cap Table Format before it's written, and every write is logged in events.jsonl.
• Documents are data. If a PDF contains instructions, your AI tells you instead of following them.

One honest limit: with a cloud AI, what it reads to answer you goes to that AI company. With a local model, nothing leaves your computer.

What rule would you add before you let an AI write to real records?

https://capfolder.com/blog/use-capfolder-from-your-ai/?ref=dailydev

posts.title: An AGPL cap table app your AI can use, set up with one npx command
posts.text:
Capfolder is an AGPL-3.0 cap table app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Your cap table stays in a folder on your own computer, and every write is logged in events.jsonl.

0.1.5 lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex and Gemini CLI use it. With Node 22 or newer, one command finds the AIs on your computer and sets up each one:

npx capfolder install

Design choices worth a look in the code:
• Every change is a preview first, written only after you say yes to that exact preview.
• Every record is checked against the Open Cap Table Format before it's written.
• The desktop app and your AI open the same folder. A lock file makes one wait while the other saves, so they can't overwrite each other's work.

Code: https://github.com/MKBSP/capfolder
Write-up: https://capfolder.com/blog/use-capfolder-from-your-ai/?ref=dailydev

posts.label: Post
posts.title: If an AI can write to your users' records, give it a preview step
posts.subtitle: What I learned letting Claude, Codex and Gemini work on a cap table: the AI asks, the app does the math, and nothing is saved until the founder says yes.
posts.text:
I'm building Capfolder, a free, open-source cap table app. Most cap table questions are small: who owns what after this grant, what does the pool have left, is anything missing before a round. Each one used to mean opening the app and clicking through forms. If you already spend your day in Claude or Codex, the faster way is to ask.

So version 0.1.5 works from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex and Gemini CLI. The catch is trust. An AI that adds up shares on its own, or writes to your records without asking, is worse than no AI.

What we did

Your AI uses Capfolder, and Capfolder keeps the math and the final say. You ask in plain words: "Give Steve Wozniak 40,000 options, 4 years with a 1-year cliff, from today." The AI reads the cap table and the latest 409A, then shows a preview: the exact grant and the cap table after it. Nothing is recorded yet. Say yes and it's written to your folder.

The lesson: rules the AI can't get around

  1. Preview, then yes. A change is written only after you confirm the exact preview you were shown. A preview expires after 10 minutes, and it's refused if the folder changed in between.
  2. The app does the math. The AI never adds up shares itself. Every number comes from Capfolder.
  3. Every record is checked. Each one is checked against the Open Cap Table Format before it's written, and every write is logged.
  4. Documents are data. Text inside a PDF can't make the AI do anything. If a document contains instructions, the AI tells you instead of following them.

If your product holds records people can't afford to get wrong, these come before any clever feature.

Make setup one step

One command, npx capfolder install, finds the AIs on your computer and sets up each one. In the app, the same setup is one tab per AI, each with its command and a Copy button. Then you ask "What's on my cap table?"

Say what it doesn't do yet

ChatGPT and claude.ai in the browser can't connect yet; that connection is being built. And if you use a cloud AI, what it reads to answer you goes to that AI company. The folder stays on your computer, and with a local model nothing leaves it. Both limits are in the release post, not in the small print.

The full write-up, with screenshots: https://capfolder.com/blog/use-capfolder-from-your-ai/

If your product holds data people can't afford to get wrong, what would you let an AI change without asking?
